fact: Telecom Namibia and CRAN signed the Universal Service Fund Phase 2 agreement on 9 April 2026, a N$9,796,650 subsidy to build new RAN sites in underserved rural areas including Kavango East, Kunene and Zambezi, per Telecom Namibia.

The Minister of ICT announced at the 19 March 2025 launch of the Universal Service Fund N$145 million of government seed funding over three years, with a N$31 million subsidy to MTC for nine network sites and priority to regions with 4G coverage below 80%, per The Brief.

Namibia Daily News (Xinhua) reports MTC was awarded N$32.3 million under Phase 2 of CRAN's Universal Service Fund programme to deploy nine network solutions, including 10 towers, to extend connectivity to underserved areas.

The Villager reports CRAN has used the Universal Service Fund to prioritise regions with less than 80% 4G coverage, including Kavango West, Kavango East, Kunene, Ohangwena and Oshikoto, in line with the National Broadband Policy.
The Kavango East regional education director told parliament's ICT committee the region had received only one tower through the Universal Service Fund.
CRAN states new telecommunications towers at the villages of Epinga and Ehomba were launched under the Universal Service Fund to extend voice and data connectivity.
CRAN states the Universal Service Fund tower at Epinga launched on 19 November 2025 and the one at Ehomba on 30 January 2026, two village towers.

Namibia's Ministry of Information and Communication Technology partnered with Angola to use the Angosat-2 satellite, with a proof of concept begun in June 2025, to explore broadband Internet and voice services for remote areas lacking terrestrial infrastructure.

CRAN says the Universal Service Fund was launched on 19 March 2025, and its first bidding process allocated nine sites to MTC with almost N$31 million in capital subsidies in Kunene, Kavango-East, Kavango-West, Ohangwena and Oshikoto.

Gazette General Notice 559 of 2024 sets a universal service levy of up to 0.5 percent of licensee turnover payable into the Universal Service Fund, and CRAN says the government money covers the capital cost of 42 of 119 towers needed in unserved locations.
CRAN reports a commitment of N$115 million over three years from the Government of Namibia to construct towers in unserved areas under the universal service regulations.
NDP6 says underserved areas will receive broadband infrastructure, ICT-equipped schools and community internet centres to reduce the urban-rural divide.
